title: Kan-fibration towers compute limits of spaces
statement: Use simplicial sets, Kan complexes, spaces, weak homotopy equivalences and coherent limiting cones from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and the infinity category of spaces from [def-coef-infinity-category-of-spaces]. A Kan fibration means a simplicial map with the right lifting property against every horn inclusion $\Lambda_i^m\hookrightarrow\Delta^m$, $m\geq1$ and $0\leq i\leq m$. Let $X_0\xleftarrow{p_0}X_1\xleftarrow{p_1}X_2\leftarrow\cdots$ be a strict inverse sequence of Kan complexes in a fixed universe, with each $p_n$ a Kan fibration. Let $X$ be its degreewise inverse limit: $X_m$ is the set of families $(x_n)_{n\geq0}$ with $x_n\in(X_n)_m$ and $p_n(x_{n+1})=x_n$, and simplicial operators act coordinatewise. Then $X$ is a Kan complex, and the cone of its projections represents a limit of the induced coherent diagram $N(\mathbb N^{\mathrm{op}})\to\mathcal S$ in the infinity category $\mathcal S$ of spaces. Equivalently the canonical map $X\to\operatorname{holim}_nX_n$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. This is natural for strict maps of towers. Empty complexes are allowed; no surjectivity on vertices is assumed.

source.place: Lemma 5.3.4.11, printed p.398 (PDF p.416), specialized to S a point and Kan fibrations (which lift all left horns); its proof identifies this case as an already fibrant tower. The coherent-limit interpretation is the space-valued homotopy-limit convention, also explained in Section 3.3.3. Read online 2026-10-17; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical comparison.

proof.text: Regard the tower as a diagram $D:I\to\mathrm{sSet}$ with $I=\mathbb N^{\mathrm{op}}$, inverse arrows all arrows, direct arrows identities, and degree $n$. Use the Kan model structure of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. In [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure], the matching category at $n>0$ has initial object the arrow $n\to n-1$: a compatible cone to all lower stages is uniquely specified by its component at $n-1$, the other components being its composites with the transition maps. Thus $M_nD=X_{n-1}$ and the matching map is $p_{n-1}$. At $n=0$ the matching object is terminal. Therefore $D$ is Reedy fibrant, including when some stages are empty.

source.place: Definition 5.1.2 and Theorem 5.1.3, printed pp.120-122: matching objects and inverse diagram model structure.

proof.text: Every direct latching category of $I$ is empty. Consequently the relative latching map of $A\to B$ at $n$ is just $A_n\to B_n$, so [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure] makes Reedy cofibrations and trivial cofibrations precisely the objectwise ones. The ordinary constant-diagram functor $c:\mathrm{sSet}\to\mathrm{sSet}^I$ therefore preserves both classes. Its right adjoint is the strict limit functor: a natural transformation $cK\to A$ is exactly a compatible family $K\to A_n$, and hence factors uniquely through the degreewise compatible-family limit. Thus $c\dashv\lim_I$ is a Quillen adjunction by [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction]. In particular $\lim_I$ preserves fibrations and terminal objects. Since $D$ is fibrant by Step 1, its strict limit $X$ is fibrant, hence Kan by [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper].

source.place: Corollary 5.1.6, printed p.123: limit is right Quillen for an inverse category; the adjunction and class check are expanded here.

proof.text: Let $W$ be weak homotopy equivalences and $W_I$ their objectwise class. Apply [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction] to $c\dashv\lim_I$. All simplicial sets are cofibrant because their initial inclusions are monomorphisms by [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], and $c$ preserves all weak equivalences, since the diagram weak equivalences are objectwise. Thus the derived left functor is the localized constant functor. Since $D$ is already Reedy fibrant, the derived right functor at $D$ is represented by its strict limit $X$. Its derived counit is represented by the ordinary counit $cX\to D$, whose components are exactly the projections. For every object $K$ of $\mathrm{sSet}[W^{-1}]_\infty$ the derived adjunction therefore gives the natural mapping-space equivalence $\operatorname{Map}(K,X)\simeq\operatorname{Map}(cK,D)$, including the projection-induced map and its coherent naturality.

source.place: Corollary 5.1.6 and the coherent derived-adjunction theorem cited in lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction; this is the mapping-space form of the right derived limit.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-small-diagram-model-rectification] to the Kan model category and the small ordinary category $I$. It identifies $\mathrm{sSet}^I[W_I^{-1}]_\infty$ with $\operatorname{Fun}(N(I),\mathrm{sSet}[W^{-1}]_\infty)$, preserving constants, the given diagram and its natural transformations. Hence the equivalence of Step 3 becomes $\operatorname{Map}(K,X)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(N(I),\mathrm{sSet}[W^{-1}]_\infty)}(\Delta K,D)$ with the projection cone. Apply the mapping-space characterization of limiting cones in [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]: the displayed equivalence is induced by composition with the projection cone, so that cone is terminal in the coherent cone category of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Identify the Kan-model localization with $\mathcal S$ by [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization]. Its simplicial-model hypothesis holds for the usual internal mapping complexes: tensor is product, all cofibrations are monos, products and pushouts are degreewise, so a pushout product of cofibrations is mono. If the second factor is trivial, write it as a retract of a transfinite composite of pushouts of horn inclusions by [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]; [lem-coef-sset-anodyne-pushout-product] makes the pushout product anodyne, and pushout products preserve retracts. If the first factor is trivial, use the symmetry isomorphism of the pushout-product construction to interchange the two factors and apply the same argument. Thus the pushout product is a trivial cofibration by the Kan model lifting-class characterization. The mapping-space adjunction turns these pushout-product lifting properties into the simplicial-model axiom. All objects are cofibrant and the fibrant objects are Kan, so the bifibrant simplicial nerve is precisely the definition of $\mathcal S$ in [def-coef-infinity-category-of-spaces]. Thus $X$ with the specified projections is a limit in that exact infinity category.

source.place: Corollary 5.1.6 for the model limit; the coherent rectification and bifibrant-nerve localization sources are those of the cited existing nodes. HTT Lemma 5.3.4.11, printed p.398, confirms the point-base result.

proof.text: The simplicial set $X$ constructed in Step 2 has in degree $m$ exactly the families $(x_n)$ satisfying $p_n(x_{n+1})=x_n$. A face or degeneracy applied coordinatewise preserves these equations because every $p_n$ is simplicial. Its projection counit is therefore the cone in the statement. For a strict transformation $a:D\to E$, the limit map sends $(x_n)$ to $(a_n(x_n))$, and $\pi_n\lim(a)=a_n\pi_n$ holds in every degree. The coherent naturality in Steps 3-4 consequently gives naturality for strict maps of towers. By the terminal-object uniqueness clause of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], its comparison with any chosen limiting cone is an equivalence of cones and hence of their apices, equivalently a weak homotopy equivalence of the representing Kan complexes. No step required a vertex to lift without a specified horn, so no vertex-surjectivity or nonemptiness hypothesis has entered.

source.place: Degreewise limit definition; naturality of the counit and of the comparisons established in Steps 3-4.

proof_origin.place: Corollary 5.1.6 and Definition 5.1.2/Theorem 5.1.3, combined with the existing coherent derived-adjunction, diagram-rectification and simplicial-model-localization nodes; explicit mapping-space argument supplied here. Agrees with HTT Lemma 5.3.4.11 at a point.
